subject: Next steps and compatibility notes for Stratos pilot (SDK / streaming / rerank)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@stratoshealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps and compatibility notes for Stratos pilot (SDK / streaming / rerank)

Hi Aisha — great conversation today. Thanks for walking us through your triage flow and the constraints around PHI handling and sub-second response expectations for the clinician UI. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of pain points you shared:
- High-latency risk when multiple records are fetched and combined per request (avg 450ms target at 95th percentile)
- Need deterministic structured output (patient_summary JSON) for downstream systems
- Desire to run an initial rerank + extract flow: candidate generation (embeddings), reranking, then structured extraction
- Compliance: SOC2 + audit log retention for inference audit (90 days)

Redwood fit / recommended config for the pilot:
- SDK changes: recommend using our v1.8 SDK (small delta upgrade) enabling streaming responses and the function-calling helper. We'll add a small helper wrapper to generate the patient_summary schema automatically.
- Function calling: use function-calls v2 to map slots to structured fields; we can provide a sample schema and type-checking hooks.
- Streaming: enable token-streaming to the UI (reduce perceived latency). For critical requests, use streaming + prefix KV caching for repeated patient prompts.
- Embeddings & rerank: generate 512-d embeddings for candidate pool; use rerank scoring with min-sim threshold 0.78 and a light-weight cross-encoder reranker for final sort.
- Performance knobs: start with batching target=6 requests @ avg 220 tokens and target batch latency 80ms; we can tune based on telemetry.

Attachments: compatibility matrix + sample patient_summary schema attached.

Action items (owners & dates):
- Redwood (Jonas): share a thin pilot playbook + small SDK diff by EOD tomorrow. (2027-07-12)
- Stratos (Aisha/Samir): confirm data access path (S3 presigned or VPC peering) and SOC2 evidence request list by Tue 7/13.
- Redwood (Marissa): schedule a 60-min technical working session next week with eng and security.

If that aligns, we’ll provision a small dedicated pool (2x A10g equiv) for the 2-week pilot and ship the SDK helper. Happy to revise if I missed anything.

Best,
Jonas

Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps and compatibility notes for Stratos pilot (SDK / streaming / rerank)

Thanks Jonas — this is very clear and helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Data path: we prefer S3 presigned URLs for the pilot (dev/staging buckets only). Samir will share a bucket policy and a short-lived presign workflow doc by EOD.
2) Audit logs: we need request-level inference logs with user-id and request-id; 90-day retention is ok. Any PII should be redacted before logs leave our VPC — is that supported?
3) Throughput: clinician UI will batch up to 3 patient records in a single request during peak; so the batching guidance you listed looks reasonable but we’ll validate with a sample trace.

We’re good to have a technical working session — request Marissa to include a short demo of the SDK helper.

Aisha
VP of Product
Stratos Health
aisha.shah@stratoshealth.com

Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps and compatibility notes for Stratos pilot (SDK / streaming / rerank)

Aisha — quick answers inline and a small ask at the bottom: 

1) S3 presigned: perfect. Samir, when you share the policy, include a sample presigned flow so we can test end-to-end.
2) Audit logs & PII: Redwood can redact specific fields before logs leave the private plane. For the pilot we’ll implement a redact hook in the SDK (local redact → logs → upload). We’ll include proof points in the security packet.
3) Throughput: understood. We’ll provision for 3-record concurrency in the pilot tuning.

Ask: can your engineering team share a 2-minute trace of a clinician session (anonymized) so we can run it through our latency model? If yes, please drop in the drive folder you mentioned.

I’ll attach the pilot playbook and a short SDK diff in the working session invite.

Thanks,
Jonas
